original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Read #2973 error description and MATH.md; manually reconstruct the prefix states of 01021323 before running any large census.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no full enumeration or mathematical validation.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Opt-in PR5001 matching-capacity integration into a source-bound successor of the maintained parity-corrected union census, restricted to its simple balanced-weight-split caller.
scope_change_reason: PR5001 already proves the capacity condition; the new question is actual engine caller compatibility, exact restored/accepted leaf preservation, and bounded runtime, not another proof of the capacity theorem.
bottleneck_link: A stronger necessary completion predicate is useful only if its live caller meets the simple-path ABI and its runtime justifies the added work.
stop_rule: Exact complete leaf receipts in n<=5,L<=12 plus bounded timing decision; no seven-label census or new kappa.
evidence: Five complete domains with exact restored/accepted leaf Counter equivalence; 436 split-kernel checks; three actual-completion semantic mutation witnesses; repeat-capable caller bypass; normal and optimized Python; bounded local timing decision retains opt-in status.
author: JoyboyBrian
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or proof-kernel review.
caller_preconditions: Capacity enabled only when the exact Hamming-weight split is S=T=L/2; no prune when that gate fails.
The existing maximum reachable distinct-size test rejects each repeated nonclosing state immediately in this target split.
Only q_0,...,q_(L-1) enter the path; q_L=0 is the final closing edge.
Each omission uses its actual functional class counts and all feasible final class splits, never the Hamming-weight target split.
success_condition: Prune off/on yields the same complete restored-word multiset, universal-hit multiset, and scientific report counts; semantic mutations are rejected.
inherited_obligations: Finite-domain equivalence is not a full multiplication theorem or supplier admission.
No claim about repeat-aware or unbalanced-weight-split searches; these bypass capacity.
No seven-label production replay, kappa update, or source-priority change.

open_questions.question: Does capacity justify enabling by default in any larger production shard?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The capacity computation may cost more than the removed search.
open_questions.first_step: Use the bounded decision here before requesting a separate resource budget for one named shard.
open_questions.blocked_by: No seven-label runtime evidence in this task.
